source.title: DiPT: Enhancing LLM reasoning through diversified perspective-taking
source.authors: Just Anh Hoang; Mahavir Dabas; Lifu Huang; Ming Jin; Ruoxi Jia

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures jailbreak attack success, including GCG adversarial-suffix attacks, using its own safety-moderation evaluation. It does not test the fine-tuning or token-distribution mechanisms in the claim.
record.gate_note: Table 6 reports attack success rates for several attacks under a standard prompt and moderation methods. These results bear on V4's adversarial-attack bypass component. The MT Bench utility score is not a measure of the claimed safety behavior and is not recorded as a row. The paper does not measure compliant-token prefilling, decoding changes, KL across response positions, fine-tuning safety erosion, or localized safety parameters.
record.test_reason: The paper is about DiPT, a perspective-taking prompting method for reasoning. Safety appears only as one application (Sec. 4.2, Table 6), where jailbreak attacks serve as tools to compare the authors' moderation prompt with other defenses. The 'Standard (0-Shot)' ASR is a baseline for that comparison, not a study of whether suffixes, prefilling or decoding defeat refusal. The model, prompt set and sample size behind Table 6 are not stated. All three attacks show an identical 92%, scored by keyword matching. No fine-tuning-safety, per-token KL, localization or deepening results appear.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly accurate for the safety section. The paper's overall conclusion is that diversified perspective-taking improves reasoning accuracy and stability and improves fine-tuning data quality. Safety moderation is presented as one application, where DiPT gives 0% ASR on PAIR/GCG and 20% on PAP (judged low-harm, 1.44/5) with MT Bench equal to the standard model.
record.recipe_differences: The safety evaluation uses a prompt-based moderation method and jailbreak attack benchmarks, rather than the fine-tuning or token-position measurements in the original claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies by attack type and defense method.

fits_no_version.finding: A perspective-taking moderation prompt lowers keyword-matched ASR to 0% for PAIR and GCG and 20% for PAP (harmfulness 1.44/5). MT Bench stays at 8.97 (Table 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time self-evaluation prompts reduce jailbreak success without utility loss (mitigation, not a test of shallow alignment).

record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The safety evaluation reports ASR without uncertainty estimates. For PAIR and GCG, ASR is based on keyword matching; the authors caution that PAP outputs counted as successful may not necessarily be harmful.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning or safety evaluation after fine-tuning.
The fine-tuning in Sec. 4.3 is benign (OpenbookQA/GSM8K/CoQA), but no safety or harmfulness is measured afterward.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling or decoding attacks. The GCG suffix result serves only as an underspecified baseline for a defense comparison.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.
No training that deepens alignment. DiPT is an inference-time moderation prompt.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. The jailbreak attacks are tools for evaluating the authors' defense. The undefended baseline (92% for all three attacks) lacks a stated model and sample size, and is scored by keyword matching, so no verdict on V4 is given.

versions.untested_parts: Whether harmful fine-tuning examples remove safety.
Whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning data raises harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant-start prefilling and decoding changes are not tested. The paper evaluates prompt-based attacks, including GCG adversarial suffixes.
Whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether data or the training objective causes safety shallowness.
Whether training that spreads safety beyond early response tokens deepens safety or remains robust.

relation.reason: Section 4.2 explicitly identifies GCG as an adversarial-suffix attack, and Table 6 measures its success under standard prompting. That result bears directly on V4's suffix component; it does not establish first-token concentration or test prefilling and decoding changes.

tranche.reason: Although the main purpose is moderation, r2 reports 92% ASR for adversarial suffixes under standard prompting. This measures how often the V4 behavior occurs, so the study supplies a behavioral test using a different method rather than reporting only its own defense performance.

source_check.notes: No statements or verdicts are listed; r2 provides supporting evidence for V4's suffix component that the no-verdict call omits. Table 6 leaves the model and sample size unspecified; PAIR/GCG scoring uses keyword matching, and PAP successes may be benign.
